title: AI UGC Video Ads Guide: What Makes One Work | AIVideosUGC
description: Plan an AI-generated creator-style product ad, check that it is not presented as a customer review, then edit the opening, scene, and final details.
h1: AI UGC Video Ads Guide: Creator-Style Clips for Your Shop
lead: UGC means user-generated content: photos or videos made by customers. An AI UGC-style ad borrows a creator-style look, but its person is AI-generated, not a real customer or reviewer. This guide covers planning the opening, describing a scene, choosing a length, and finishing product videos for TikTok, Reels, or Shorts.
secondary_keywords: short video ads for small brands
summary: A plain-English walkthrough of creator-style video ads: the opening shot, the scene description, length, size, and finishing touches.

paras: Here, creator-style describes the camera and setting: handheld framing, an ordinary kitchen, bathroom, desk, or car, and a product shown in natural light. The person is AI-generated, so the video is not a real customer's review or endorsement.

Sellers use this style on [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok), [Instagram](page:plat-instagram) Reels, and [YouTube Shorts](page:plat-youtube-shorts) because it fits beside the posts people are already scrolling past. It shows the product in someone's hands or a familiar setting, adding another view alongside a polished studio shot.

In [AIVideosUGC Video Ads](page:video-ads), you upload a product photo, write one sentence about the scene, and get a short clip of 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. There's no filming to arrange and no samples to ship out. For a still companion to the clip, try [lifestyle product photos](page:lifestyle-photos) in the same everyday setting.

sections.h2: Plan the first second before anything else
paras: People decide quickly whether to keep watching, so the opening frame should already show the product doing something. Try not to start on an empty room or on a person with nothing in their hands.

Some opening ideas for different products: a reusable water bottle pulled out of a gym bag and tipped back for a drink; a phone case snapped onto a phone, then tossed onto a sofa cushion; a rope toy thrown across a living room for a dog; [a serum dropper squeezed over the back of a hand](page:tpl-beauty).

Stick to one main action per clip. A 10-second video has room for one clear moment and a little context, not a whole story. Planning your first TikTok ad? Start with [Your First TikTok Video Ad](page:guide-first-tiktok-video-ad).

sections.h2: Write the scene in one sentence
paras: Your sentence is all the video has to go on, so make it count. Cover four things: who is in the shot, where they are, what they do with the product, and how it's filmed.

Here's an example for a cold brew bottle: "A woman in her 30s at a sunny kitchen counter pours iced coffee from our glass bottle into a tall glass, filmed handheld on a phone." And one for a backpack: "A college student unzips our gray backpack on a library table and pulls out a laptop, close-up, natural window light." Food and drink sellers can find more scene ideas on our [food and drinks page](page:ind-food-drinks).
Leave out any words you want on screen, famous faces, and logos that aren't yours. Requests like these may be refused, and lettering drawn by AI is likely to come out wrong anyway.

sections.h2: Choose a length and a shape
paras: Six seconds is enough for a single action, like a lid twisting off. Ten seconds fits an action plus a second angle or a reaction. Fifteen seconds lets you show a short sequence, such as taking the product out, using it, and setting it down. Thirty seconds gives a longer demonstration room to breathe.

For TikTok, Reels, and Shorts, pick 9:16 so the video fills the phone screen. Use 1:1 for square feed placements and 16:9 for a regular YouTube video or a wide banner on your product page. You can also pick 3:4 or 4:3. The [ad sizes guide](page:guide-ad-sizes-by-platform) shows where each shape fits.
Videos are made one at a time. If you want another version with a different opening or setting, generate it as a new video; the credit cost appears before each one starts.

sections.h2: Finish the ad in your editing app
paras: Think of the clip you download as raw footage. Captions, music, your price, a discount code, and a line like "Shop the new colors" all go on afterward in CapCut, TikTok, Canva, or Ads Manager. Adding them yourself keeps the spelling and numbers right.

Keep on-screen text short, and keep it away from the bottom and right edges of a vertical video, where the caption, likes, and comment buttons sit. The upper middle of the frame is a safer spot for your main line.

sections.h2: Make a few versions and let your results decide
paras: A single video doesn't tell you much. Make two or three that change just one thing, such as the opening action, the setting, or the person, and [run them side by side](page:guide-testing-ad-versions) in your ad account with the same budget and audience.

Once each has had a fair amount of spend, compare how long people watched and how many clicked through. Keep the stronger one, change one more thing, and run it again. Over time you'll learn which kinds of scenes suit your product.

faq.q: Can I say the person in the video is a real customer?
faq.a: No. The person in the clip is generated by AI, so don't give them a name, a backstory, or a quote that suggests they bought and reviewed your product. Keep your captions focused on what the product is and how it's used.

faq.q: How long should a UGC-style video ad be?
faq.a: Start with 6 or 10 seconds for a single moment, like picking up the product and showing it to the camera. Use 15 seconds when the clip needs to show the product being used.

faq.q: What should I add after downloading an AI UGC ad?
faq.a: Add accurate captions, price, offer, music, and disclosure in TikTok, CapCut, Canva, or Ads Manager. The generated clip does not supply those items.

faq.q: What length works for an AI UGC ad?
faq.a: Use 6 seconds for one product beat, 10 or 15 seconds for a short demo, and 30 seconds only where the public option is available.
